label: EXPERIMENTAL / OOD
question: Can recent season-local scoring residuals improve J1 first exact and ordered three scores by correcting the goal-total distribution?
motivation: R25's 150-match 2026/27 archive shows 2.70 R7 expected goals versus 2.87 realized and produced the same first scores as R7 at its selected dose. This motivates a separate total-goals experiment. All these dates are historical development evidence.
common_sources_and_windows: Use the byte-locked R25 protocol for the R5 panel, R7 model and original firsts, weekend plan, and the exact regular J1 fixture windows. Fit on 2,291 games through 2024, select on 218 in the first half of 2025, then evaluate 162 in the rest of 2025 and 150 in 2026/27. Use each window's original records and compare the R25, R7 and market forecasts on the same fixture identities. No post-fit tuning on either evaluation window.
features: Use R7 chronological pregame anchors. For earlier same-season regular J1 games compute observed 90-minute total minus anchor mean total, clipped to [-4,4]. After each full match date update the season and both participating team histories. Decay residual sums and counts with a 45-day half-life. The league contrast divides its residual sum by exposure plus 20. For each team divide by its exposure plus 8. Clip contrasts to [-1,1] and take the arithmetic mean of the two club contrasts. A missing earlier history is neutral. Features are intercept, league contrast, team mean contrast. No target-day completion enters any feature. R7 remains scoped as originally archived.
method: Fit three slopes on chronological anchors in the training window. For each total t multiply its existing probability by exp(min(t,8) * X beta), then normalize. Fit summed total-goals negative log likelihood plus 16 times sum of squared coefficients, with per-coefficient absolute bounds 0.15, 0.25, 0.25. Normalize the whole adjusted grid with one factor so conditional score allocation at each total remains the same. Use the original locked R7 post-fit prior for validation and evaluation. Keep the original archived R7 WDL and actual-line totals decisions; rerank only the three displayed score cells. Return the original R7 score picks exactly at zero change.
selection: Compare blend doses 0, 0.5, 1. On the 218 validation rows require neither first hits nor ordered-three hits below original R7. Choose lexicographically by first hits, ordered-three hits, negative exact-score log loss and smaller dose. Report all validation trials, the selected and full-dose historical evaluation, per-window paired gains and losses with match-day bootstrap intervals, coverage and all four metrics. Leave archived missing lines and markets in coverage.
forward: If selected dose is positive and the combined evaluation has a gain in at least one of first and ordered-three and no loss in either versus R7, refit only the three coefficients through the pinned Nov 21 panel, keep the locked dose, and issue the complete Nov 28/29 slate once the schedule is validated. Use the original R5 inputs, original locked R7 post-fit prior and signed R7 control, with source and real clocks intact. Freeze research predictions and separately rank three seats by p(first), kickoff then match ID. Missing market remains missing. Keep the original comprehensive first-display window independent and report actual upcoming coverage and strict market readiness. If the screen fails, finish the numerical recipe in historical development and continue independent first-display verification work. None of these historical samples can certify stage 1.
